critical_code_review_comments: TASK A H1 IS EXCELLENT: The balanced-brace scanner with in_string / escape tracking is the correct fix — a naive regex or first-{/last-} approach cannot handle nested braces inside quoted strings. The scanner emits ALL top-level {…} blocks and tries the LARGEST first, so a preamble '{...}' won't shadow the real report. Verified via the string-with-braces-inside test where '{"quote": "he said \"hello { world }\" today"}' parses correctly.

TASK A H1 SMART: The fenced-block regex `\`\`\`(?:json|JSON)?\s*(\{.*?\})\s*\`\`\`` with re.DOTALL correctly captures the object payload even if it spans lines. Using max(fences, key=len) is a nice touch — a common Gemini failure mode is to emit an example fence and then the real one; the real one is always larger.
TASK A H1 SUBTLE: Trailing-comma regex `,(\s*[}\]])` runs AFTER candidate selection, so it only fires on the candidate the walker chose — safer than blanket rewriting the whole text.

TASK A H2 CORRECT: Retry uses a fresh LlmChat with a NEW session_id (`{session_id}-retry`), preventing the poisoned previous turn from being re-sent as context. The strict prompt front-loads the constraint. Retry timeout is preserved (240 s extra_params + 300 s wait_for), matching the primary call.

TASK A H2 GOOD ERROR SHAPE: 502 is semantically correct here — Gemini is an upstream dependency, and its bad output IS a bad gateway response. The user-facing message ('short videos, unusual angles, or heavy motion blur') is actionable — much better than the old opaque 500. Frontend can safely render analysis_error verbatim.

MINOR SUGGESTION (not blocking): The retry path re-uses `file_contents` (the base64-encoded video is re-sent). For a rate-limited failure mode this doubles bandwidth. Acceptable because JSON-formatting failures are rare and the retry is bounded to 1 attempt.

TASK B I1 CLEAN: The conditional `(strengths?.length || dev?.length || concern?.length)` correctly gates rendering — if scout_view has all three arrays empty we hide the whole grid rather than showing two 'empty' cards. Empty-state italic fallback INSIDE each card handles the case where ONLY one of the two lists is empty. Good defensive UX.

TASK B I1 GOOD: Fallback chain is `development_priorities?.length ? development_priorities : areas_of_concern` — using ?.length (not just ?) means an empty array falls through to concerns. This matches the semantic: 'if we have proper development priorities, use them; otherwise show the older areas_of_concern'.

TASK B I4 VISUAL: Screenshot shows the pinned cards land visually between the 8-pillar breakdown and the radar hero. That's actually a nicer position than 'immediately above the radar' — parents scanning the report land on the two pinned verdicts right after the pillars, and the radar reinforces them. Session 123 delivered.

rca of the issue: Original production bug 46c460d8: extract_json used naive text.find('{')..text.rfind('}'), which fails on ANY response with prose containing curly braces (e.g. 'The {player} showed …'), smart quotes ('vs "), trailing commas (Python-legal, JSON-illegal), or multiple fences (grabbed the wrong one). Fix (verified): tolerant scanner with (a) BOM/zero-width strip, (b) smart-quote normalization to ASCII, (c) largest-fence preference, (d) balanced-brace walker with in-string/escape tracking so string-embedded { doesn't confuse depth, (e) trailing-comma repair via regex sub, (f) categorized ValueError with prefix so caller can decide retry policy, (g) retry-once with fresh LlmChat + stricter system_message + prepended IMPORTANT: instruction, (h) HTTPException(502) with actionable user-facing message on double-fail. Any of the 46c460d8-class responses would now either (i) parse on first attempt, (ii) parse on retry after the strict prompt, or (iii) return an actionable 502 telling the user 'try again with a clearer clip' instead of the useless 500 'invalid format'.
